items.informal_name: Weighted Order Upper Bound for Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f ≠ 0 → MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f ≤ ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if the coefficient of a monomial $ d $ in $ f $ is non-zero, then the weighted order of $ f $ is less than or equal to the weight of $ d $, i.e., $ \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(f) \leq \sum_{i \in \operatorname{support} d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted order of a multivariate power series
items.type: {σ : Type u_1} → {R : Type u_2} → [Semiring R] → (σ → ℕ) → MvPowerSeries σ R → ℕ∞
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, the weighted order of $ f $ is the minimal natural number $ n $ such that there exists a monomial $ d $ with non-zero coefficient in $ f $ where the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $ equals $ n $. If $ f $ is the zero series, the weighted order is $ \top $ (infinity).

items.informal_name: Lower Bound on Weighted Order of Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {n : ℕ∞},
  (∀ (d : σ →₀ ℕ), ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d) < n → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0) → n ≤ MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f
items.informal_description: For any extended natural number $n$, if every monomial $d$ with $\text{weight}(w, d) < n$ has zero coefficient in the multivariate power series $f$, then $n \leq \text{weightedOrder}(f, w)$, where $\text{weightedOrder}(f, w)$ denotes the weighted order of $f$ with respect to the weight function $w$.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order Lower Bound for Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {n : ℕ},
  (∀ (d : σ →₀ ℕ), (Finsupp.weight w) d < n → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0) → ↑n ≤ MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if every monomial $ d $ with weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) < n $ has zero coefficient in $ f $, then the weighted order of $ f $ with respect to $ w $ satisfies $ n \leq \text{weightedOrder}_w(f) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order of Product of Multivariate Power Series Bounds Sum of Individual Weighted Orders
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {ι : Type u_4} (w : σ → ℕ) (f : ι → MvPowerSeries σ R)
  (s : Finset ι), ∑ i ∈ s, MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (f i) ≤ MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (∏ i ∈ s, f i)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of multivariate power series over a commutative semiring $ R $, indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, the sum of the weighted orders of each series in $ s $ is less than or equal to the weighted order of their product. If the product is the zero series, its weighted order is $ \top $ (infinity).

items.informal_name: Coefficients of Multivariate Power Series with Weight Below Weighted Order Are Zero
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d) < MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f → (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f = 0
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $ of a monomial $ d $ is strictly less than the weighted order of $ f $, then the coefficient of $ d $ in $ f $ is zero. The weighted order of $ f $ is defined as the minimal natural number $ n $ such that there exists a monomial with non-zero coefficient in $ f $ whose weighted sum equals $ n $. If $ f $ is the zero series, its weighted order is $ \top $ (infinity).
